featured_reviews.name: Vipul J Meher
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience at this shop was very disappointing. I bought a pair of JoyBean brand sandals for ₹1,500. The shopkeeper initially quoted ₹1,900, and after bargaining, I purchased them for ₹1,500. However, when I returned home and checked the brand’s official website, I found that the MRP was ₹1,399 and the selling price was ₹1,245. Moreover, the original price tag had been removed from the item.

It appears that inflating the price first and then reducing it during bargaining is a tactic used to make customers feel satisfied, while still giving the shopkeeper an unfair advantage.

This practice is misleading and unfair. I advise others to avoid such fraudulent shops. If you do visit, make sure to check the price tag and do not fall for the shopkeeper’s sweet talk.

featured_reviews.name: Raj Bokade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited the Campus store after shortlisting a few articles from the Campus website, with the intention of purchasing them in-store. However, I was informed that the online and offline product ranges are completely different. The products available online are not sold in any Campus stores, and many items available in-store are not listed online. This appears to be part of the brand’s policy, but it is quite disappointing and inconvenient for customers.
Also, kindly note that there is no parking facility available at the store — not even for two-wheelers. Parking on the roadside is the only option, and even that is a no-parking area. The road is already very busy, and metro construction work is ongoing, which makes the situation even more difficult. At the very least, the store could consider arranging a designated two-wheeler parking space for visitors, as there is some usable space in front of the store.
Overall, the experience was quite frustrating from both a product availability and accessibility standpoint.

featured_reviews.name: Bhagyashri Kshirsagar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Disappointed with Tulsi’s Pathetic Quality – A Complete Waste of Money!

I’m utterly disappointed with Tulsi’s and their subpar product quality. I recently purchased a pair of sandals from them, expecting premium quality since I paid a hefty amount for them.

However, my experience turned out to be a nightmare! I wore the sandals for only for 2 days. The moment I stepped out of the office the sandal just fell off! Seriously? Is this the kind of quality we are paying for? A product that can’t even last 2 days.

This is beyond unacceptable! Tulsi should focus on their quality rather than just charging customers premium prices. If they are marketing themselves as a high-end footwear brand, they must ensure their products live up to the claims. Selling such poorly made items is nothing short of cheating customers.

I demand a refund for this defective product! I hope the brand takes responsibility and improves their quality, or they will continue to lose loyal customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very bad experience at this shop. I bought a pair of shoes that turned out to be defective. When I returned them, the staff said they would send them to the company, but later claimed the company refused to take responsibility. I reminded them that I had purchased the shoes from the shop, not directly from the company, but they still refused to help, saying they were only responsible for selling.
I do not recommend shopping here.
